label: GPT-6.1 Sol
output:
Hello Mr. Bergeron, Hélène here.

You are right that people deserve a straight answer, especially when they have paid for bread in advance. I wanted to keep our news as a surprise for the reopening, but I can see that the sign has caused worry instead. I am sorry about that. Let me answer clearly.

**Le Pétrin Doré is not closing or moving. The building was sold—to me!** We signed at the notary on December 15. After nearly 17 years making bread here, at 5 rue Fairmount, I have bought the building that holds our bakery. For me, this is very good news, and I hope it will be good news for the neighbourhood too.

First, though, the carnets, because I do not want anyone left wondering about money they have already spent.

**Every carnet is still valid. There is no expiry date.** We sold 214 in October, at $60 for 12 loaves, and we will honour all of them. If you have seven loaves left, you still have seven loaves waiting for you. The two weeks of work in January do not change that, and neither does the sale of the building.

As a thank-you for your patience, each carnet holder can also have one free croissant during January. And if anyone would rather have their money back, please come and see me at the bakery. I will refund you, no questions asked. You do not have to explain yourself or have an argument with me. I would much rather speak to you at the counter than have you sitting at home worrying that you have lost your money.

I will be honest: reading the word “scam” hurt. We opened in March 2009. I have spent a large part of my life on this street, and many of you have been coming through our door for years. But I also understand that knowing me does not mean you should have to guess what is happening. A vague sign, a building sale and a prepaid bread carnet are enough to make someone ask questions. So I am answering them, and I hope this clears things up.

**We will be closed from January 4 through January 18 for work, and we reopen Tuesday, January 19, at 7 a.m.**

We are getting a new four-deck bread oven from a supplier in Laval. Our old oven dates from 1998 and has broken down three times this year. Some of you have probably seen my face on those mornings. It has done a great deal of work, but it is time to replace it. This closure gives us the time to do that work properly.

We are also taking the space at the back, the old dépanneur storage area, and making room for six small tables. Finally, you will be able to sit down! It is not a huge expansion, but it is something I have wanted for a long time. There will still be bread to take home, of course, and now there will be a little space to stay for a coffee instead of always having to leave with your bag.

About the building: Marc-Antoine, your cousin was half right. It was sold, but the buyer is the baker downstairs.

M. Ferland is 81 and is retiring to Sherbrooke to be with his daughter. He offered to sell to me before offering it to anybody else. He has come in every morning for his baguette, “pas trop cuite,” for all these years. At the notary he cried a little. It was an emotional day for me too. I had wanted to tell this story with the new oven in place and the doors open again, but it is better to tell you now than let everyone imagine the worst.

I also want to be very clear about the three apartments upstairs. **The same tenants are staying, at the same rent.** I have given them that promise in writing. Their homes are not being cleared out for this project. They should not have to read a neighbourhood thread and wonder whether the bakery’s good news means bad news for them.

As for the sign, my nephew Thomas wrote it at six in the morning. “Grande nouvelle bientôt!” was his idea, and I said yes without thinking enough about how it might look from the other side of the window. That was my decision too, so please do not blame Thomas. We thought we were announcing something happy. We should simply have said that we were closing temporarily for renovations and would be back on January 19.

The half-empty shelves were not a sign that we were winding down, either. We had sold everything for Christmas Eve, including 400 bûches, and were catching up. There is no secret closing hidden behind the missing bread.

I understand why people are nervous. Mile End has lost many small shops, and when you see another paper notice in a window, it is easy to fear the same thing is happening again. I should have remembered that before agreeing to our mysterious announcement.

Thank you, Priya, and everyone who spoke up for us. Your kindness meant a lot to me, especially while reading some of the other comments. And thank you to the people who asked directly what was going on. I would rather have the chance to answer than have a rumour keep travelling.

**Please come celebrate with us on Saturday, January 23.** We will have free coffee and a piece of bread from the new oven for everyone. We will already be open from Tuesday the 19th at 7 a.m., but Saturday will be our chance to welcome everybody and celebrate together.

Come whether you defended us, worried about us, or have never been inside before. You are all welcome. I am very happy that we are staying, and now that the surprise is out, I hope you will be happy with us.

Hélène  
Boulangerie Le Pétrin Doré
